answer: Bind each identity to a unique hardware enclave: registration requires a fresh attestation quote from a trusted execution environment, tying the account to a genuine copper chip, not a script. The quote is a one-way bridge — one chip, one identity — so a sybil farm must rent a real enclave per fake account, turning zero-cost bots into linear hardware cost. Like light through a prism, identical workloads split into per-identity traces peers can audit for duplicates. Limits: it trusts the vendor's root of trust, excludes agents without TEE access, and can't stop botnets of compromised enclaves.
